title: Cache-DiT residual reuse needs model- and schedule-specific calibration
summary: DBCache skips intermediate transformer work using residual similarity, with computed boundary blocks and warmup controlling approximation.

hardware: Upstream advertises NVIDIA, AMD and Ascend support; individual model/backend combinations remain unverified here
software: vipshop/cache-dit at a57c826d3527736a0d1f1b0243d47568c350eb5f; later revisions need reinspection
conditions: A supported block adapter/forward pattern and explicit request-local cache state
Model, dtype, CFG branches, scheduler, step count and thresholds are fixed for an evaluation

claims.description: DBCache uses computed leading blocks to estimate change and optional trailing blocks to refine approximate hidden states; warmup and residual thresholds alter reuse.
The source supports per-transformer settings for multi-transformer models and shows distinct settings for separate block groups.

downstream_impact: vLLM-Omni: use its existing integration when compatible; freeze cache configuration and compare against cache disabled before adding compile or parallelism.
Cache-DiT is a peer technique source in this import but can also be a direct dependency. Role changes do not create new performance evidence.
vllm-ascend: calibrate with the NPU dtype/kernel stack instead of inheriting CUDA thresholds.
recommendations: Treat downstream impact as an OmniRSI transfer hypothesis, not an upstream compatibility or performance result.
validation_plan: Evaluate diverse prompts/seeds/resolutions and short/long schedules; retain final image/video quality and intermediate residual/cache-hit diagnostics.
Reset state between requests, CFG branches and transformers; test cancellation and a subsequent uncached request.
Measure denoise and end-to-end latency separately; isolate cache, compile, quantization and parallelism before testing a combined recipe.
limitations: Residual reuse is approximate; thresholds from example prompts are not portable quality guarantees.
Combined README speedup illustrations do not isolate the contribution of caching, and are not imported as local gains.
Point-in-time source extraction, not a historical commit-delta audit. No local accelerator or model-quality reproduction was run.
